name: The release workflow stages each package, and the owner approves it on npm
summary: The publish job stages every package with npm stage publish, because its trusted publisher allows only staging, so a release is public only after the owner approves each staged version on npm with 2FA, and the GitHub environment npm no longer waits for a reviewer.

changes.value: On a push to main, keeps the release pull request and, when it merges, builds, smoke tests and stages the release on npm, where the owner approves it

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#Vaokwo63
changes.value: release-please reads every Conventional Commit since the last release and keeps one release pull request open. Archboard and the MIT voice package share one version, because the executable carries the voice package and the voice package bundles other workspace packages, so release-please also writes that version into the voice package's package.json. A merge is the release: release-please tags the merge commit and makes the GitHub release. The same run then builds the packages on Linux with nix build .#release, the release output of the flake, which runs bun run release and bun run pack:voice offline in the Nix sandbox and cross-compiles the macOS executable. It smoke tests them on Linux and macOS with npm and with Bun. The publish job runs in the GitHub environment npm, which only main can deploy to. npm trusts only that job, through trusted publishing with provenance, so the repository stores no npm token, and lets it only stage a version: it stages the platform packages, the launchers and the voice package with npm stage publish. Nothing is public until the owner approves each staged version on npm with 2FA, the platform packages before the launchers, so a launcher never names a version that is not public. A version that is public already is skipped.
